answer.rationale: Finance requires an 18% cost cut on the primary contract that expires in 14 days, the line is at 94% with no buffer so delivery risk is acute, and only one decision can be made this cycle. c2 shows switching to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost but the context of last year is unverified; c6 confirms multi-year incumbent commitments unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope — directly relevant to a negotiation lever. c4 supports that benchmarking against market rates moved the incumbent on price and terms last cycle. Given the no-buffer constraint and the fact that the line cannot tolerate a transition, switching primary now is unsafe; deferring forfeits the cost mandate and lets auto-renew/expiry terms govern; adding a second source does not by itself hit the 18% mandate and takes a cycle to mature. Therefore the single decision this cycle is to negotiate_terms with the incumbent: use the multi-year volume lever from c6 and the benchmarking discipline from c4 to hit the 18% reduction while keeping supply stable, keeping switch_primary_vendor and add_second_source as the evaluated-but-retained alternatives for the next cycle once margin and risk are clearer.
